messages:
samir: Tried working from the garden today using a small solar generator + inverter to keep devices alive. Laptop fine but the ISP modem kept dropping every few minutes. Zoom cut out twice. Anyone here household power/solar-savvy? pic: https://i.imgur.com/solaroffice2.jpg :grimacing:

lena: ouch. is the modem on the inverter's battery-backed output or directly on the generator output? some inverters do a transfer that looks like a blink to network gear.

samir: modem plugged into the inverter output (limited outlets). inverter status says it does a 'transfer' when panels fluctuate. I saw short voltage dips.

devon: recommendation: get a tiny line-interactive UPS for the modem only. those handle sags better than straight inverter output.

jordan: +1. also check modem logs for ppp disconnects, and enable auto-reconnect on the modem/bridge. sometimes adding a short delay before bringing up pppd helps.

samir: grabbed modem log snippet via serial: ```May 04 09:48:02 pppd[2112]: pppd 2.4.7 started by root, uid 0
May 04 09:48:23 pppd[2112]: Connection terminated.
May 04 09:48:24 pppd[2112]: Exit.```

maria-g: some inverters have 'eco' or 'frequency-shift' modes to save battery that cause small interruptions. physical separation from the inverter (put modem on UPS) usually fixes it.

devon: for a cheap test, power the modem from a phone charger+powerbank (if modem accepts 5V USB) or borrow a UPS for a day. if the dropouts stop, it's definitely the inverter transfer.

wifi-bot: network-health: packet loss detected between 09:48:20-09:48:26, 0/4 pings to 8.8.8.8. latency spikes before and after event.

lena: another trick: if your modem supports it, enable DHCP 'always-on' or disable PPP enforcement so the modem keeps the link; then let the router handle reconnection.

samir: thanks! ordering a small APC UPS tonight. Also: my fern survived my experimental energy setup so there's that win :herb: :joy: (photo has suspiciously proud coffee mug)
